stem: A stone causes colicky flank pain and microscopic haematuria as it passes from the renal pelvis toward the bladder. Which structure is being obstructed?

options.label: A
options.explanation: It is the muscular tube transporting urine from the renal pelvis to the bladder and can produce flank-to-groin colic when obstructed.

options.label: B
options.explanation: It carries urine from the bladder to the exterior and would produce distal urinary symptoms.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Arterial obstruction causes ischaemia rather than urinary colic with haematuria from a travelling stone.

options.label: D
options.explanation: It is a venous conduit and does not carry urine.

options.label: E
options.explanation: Its obstruction produces pancreatic rather than urinary symptoms.

context: The ureter carries urine from kidney to bladder and has predictable narrowings where stones may lodge.
